claims.title: Classical-mediation boundary and acquired conditional entanglement test

quoted_fields.interface:
Structural coefficient contract: m finite-dimensional parties, one nonconstant local Hermitian A_i per party, real symmetric U, C=R+iJ>=0 with R real symmetric and J real antisymmetric. Generator L(rho)=-i[(1/2)sum_ij U_ij A_i A_j,rho]+sum_ij C_ij(A_i rho A_j-(1/2){A_i A_j,rho}). Commuting local Hamiltonians are allowed. Known specified coefficients for the structural decision problem; classical mediation means LOCC without pre-existing shared entanglement. This differs from the later raw-record discovery interface.

Raw-record discovery contract: Known qubit structure,trusted local preparation/analysis controls and private fresh random choices unavailable through a separate side channel. Detector POVM may be joint,coherent,correlated and history dependent under the declared current-choice contract. For a reduced-source claim require source-detector independence conditional on observed past. With shared classical flags,the null must require source FULL separability conditional on EVERY flag. No initial source-detector entanglement alone is insufficient. Discard independent local Z-phase keys permanently before subsequent evolution;they must not be recovered to undo the preparation. Local rotations preserve the resulting initial conditional product-mixture property. This is not a pure reset or guaranteed polarization.
quoted_fields.failure: The structural theorem assumes finite-dimensional parties, one nonconstant local Hermitian observable per party, commuting bilinear interactions and correlated Markovian dephasing. It does not cover arbitrary Lindbladians, noncommuting local operator families, non-Markovian mediators or unbounded target observables. The coefficient-based SDP and raw-record test have different access contracts. Trusted local controls, known qubit structure, private randomization, corrected source-detector conditions and physical preparation resources remain necessary. Unknown detector response can erase power. No exact polynomial-bit decision near an ill-conditioned SDP boundary, estimator advantage over the same-moment covariance SDP or general dominance over measurement-device-independent witnesses is claimed.
